research.notes:
**Tenet Healthcare (THC), news for 2026-09-29 to 2026-10-29**

**1. Guidance and results**
- Tenet raised its FY26 adjusted EBITDA outlook to $5.05–5.20B, up $195M at the midpoint. It also raised its adjusted free cash flow outlook by $100M. — 2026-10-29 — https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000070318/000007031826000045/thc-20260930ex991earningsr.htm
- Free cash flow range, two figures. The 8-K headline gives $2.825–3.125B (same URL as above). Another source gives $1.93–2.16B, which looks like the figure after noncontrolling interests. — 2026-10-29 — https://rallies.ai/news/tenet-healthcare-q3-revenue-beats-on-same-store-sales-growth-cddfa1e9918264ec
- Other FY26 guidance: revenue $22.05–22.45B and adjusted EPS $22.05–23.01. — 2026-10-29 — https://rallies.ai/news/tenet-healthcare-q3-revenue-beats-on-same-store-sales-growth-cddfa1e9918264ec
- Q3 adjusted EPS was $6.64, against $3.70 a year earlier. Q3 adjusted EBITDA was $1.355B, and Ambulatory Care adjusted EBITDA was $537M. — 2026-10-29 — https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000070318/000007031826000045/thc-20260930ex991earningsr.htm
- Q3 versus expectations. The consensus EPS estimate varies by source:
  - Zacks consensus was $4.60 on revenue of $5.47B. — https://www.tradingview.com/news/zacks:3388fb9bf094b:0-can-tenet-healthcare-beat-q3-earnings-on-ambulatory-care-strength/
  - Investing.com consensus was $4.67 on revenue of $5.49B. — https://www.investing.com/news/earnings/tenet-healthcare-earnings-loom-as-investors-eye-2027-outlook-93CH-4980071
  - StockStory says EPS was 42% above consensus and revenue was $5.63B. It says the FY revenue guidance midpoint ($22.25B) was 0.8% below consensus. Shares fell 1.9% to $263.50 after the report. — 2026-10-29 — https://stockstory.org/us/stocks/nyse/thc/news/earnings/tenet-healthcare-nysethc-exceeds-q3-2026-expectations
- Quality of the beat: Q3 EBITDA included a $147M net favorable impact from the Conifer revenue cycle management (RCM) transition. Contract transition activities are expected to add about $450M to FY26 EBITDA. That amount is not expected to recur in 2027. — 2026-10-29 — https://rallies.ai/news/tenet-healthcare-q3-revenue-beats-on-same-store-sales-growth-cddfa1e9918264ec

**2. Analyst actions**
- Guggenheim (Jason Cassorla) raised its price target to $307 from $283 and kept Buy. — 2026-10-16 — https://www.investing.com/news/analyst-ratings/guggenheim-raises-tenet-healthcare-stock-price-target-on-momentum-93CH-4954060
- Raymond James initiated with a Buy and a $285 target, per Investing.com, which says "late September". The exact date isn't given. A MarketBeat-syndicated item instead lists a reiteration of Outperform with a $285 target on 2026-08-14, so the initiation date is unconfirmed. — date unknown — https://www.investing.com/news/earnings/tenet-healthcare-earnings-loom-as-investors-eye-2027-outlook-93CH-4980071 and https://www.dailypolitical.com/2026/10/27/tenet-healthcare-thc-projected-to-release-quarterly-earnings-on-thursday.html

- I found no post-earnings target changes in the results, which were published on the earnings day.

**3. Litigation and regulation**
- A former employee sued Tenet. The suit says its $25-per-pay-period tobacco surcharge breaks wellness-program rules. — reported 2026-10-19 (filing date not stated) — https://news.bloomberglaw.com/employee-benefits/ex-tenet-healthcare-employee-files-suit-over-tobacco-use-penalty

writeup.headline: Tenet rates Buy on strong trend, low absolute multiples and solid margins, but sits just above Hold.
writeup.thesis: Tenet scores 66, a Buy, but only 2 points above the Hold line. The strongest supports are trend (85), with the price 22.4% above its 200-day average and shares 40.0 pp ahead of SPY over the last 126 trading days, and valuation (79). In absolute terms the multiples are low: P/FCF of 7.2x, EV/EBIT of 7.2x and an FCF yield 9.0 pp above the 10-year Treasury yield. Against its own history the valuation sits near the middle, and the multiples disagree: P/S is more expensive than at 58 of the last 61 month-ends, while P/FCF is cheaper than at 42 of the last 61 month-ends. Quality (77) is helped by a 20.8% operating margin, a 13.9% FCF margin and the diluted share count down 8.5% year on year. Growth is middling at 50, with TTM revenue growth of 5.4%, and the balance sheet is the weak spot at 35, with net debt at 3.66 times FCF and cash covering only 0.16 of debt.
key_risks: Leverage: net debt is 3.66 times FCF and cash-to-debt is only 0.16.
Part of the raised FY2026 outlook comes from roughly $450M of one-time Conifer transition benefits that will not recur in 2027.
The CommonSpirit RCM wind-down at Conifer carries a known 2027 EBITDA headwind.
Lower exchange admissions remain a payer-mix headwind.
The price is 4.4% below its 52-week high after a strong run, so the trend score could fade quickly.
what_would_change: A drop of just 2 points would move the rating to Hold, for example from weaker trend or news scores.
Reaching Strong Buy needs 14 more points, likely from stronger growth than TTM revenue growth of 5.4% or from a better balance sheet score.
Paying down debt to improve net debt to FCF and cash-to-debt would lift the weakest factor.
Signs that the 2027 Conifer headwinds hit results harder than expected would pressure growth, quality and news scores.
